title: Acetaminophen Dosing Tables for Fever and Pain in Children (table notes: frequency, under-2 rule, extra strength and extended-release limits)
org: American Academy of Pediatrics (HealthyChildren.org); Council on Quality Improvement and Patient Safety, Committee on Drugs and Committee on Practice and Ambulatory Medicine
licence_note: Copyright 2026 American Academy of Pediatrics. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16 (page last updated 1/30/2026): for children under 12 years give every 4 hours while symptoms last; do not give more than 5 doses in 24 hours; over 12 years extra strength every 6 hours, no more than 6 extra strength tablets/gelcaps in 24 hours; not under 2 years without a doctor's guidance; no 500 mg extra strength under 12; no 650 mg extended-release under 18; print-friendly chart is the pictographic PDF (key american-academy-of-pediatrics-healthychildren-org-a-b3b884).

title: Ibuprofen Dosing Table for Fever and Pain (table notes: under 6 months, frequency, adult dose)
org: American Academy of Pediatrics (HealthyChildren.org); Council on Quality Improvement and Patient Safety
licence_note: Copyright 2023 American Academy of Pediatrics. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16 (page last updated 9/19/2024): do not use ibuprofen in children less than 6 months old unless the child's doctor says to; best not to give multi-ingredient medicines under 6 years; you can give ibuprofen every 6 to 8 hours if needed; adult dose 400 mg. The print-friendly chart (key american-academy-of-pediatrics-healthychildren-org-i-076a13) says every 6 hours, no more than 4 doses in 24 hours.

title: CHILDRENS BENADRYL ALLERGY (diphenhydramine hydrochloride) oral solution, 12.5 mg/5 mL: Drug Facts label
org: DailyMed (US National Library of Medicine); labeling supplied by the manufacturer (Kenvue Brands LLC)
licence_note: Manufacturer's FDA-required Drug Facts labeling as posted on DailyMed (SPL version 15, published Oct 09, 2026). Read by R15 on 2026-11-16: Do not use to make a child sleepy; do not use with any other product containing diphenhydramine; children under 2 years: do not use; children 2 to 5 years: do not use unless directed by a doctor; store between 20-25 C (68-77 F).

title: IMODIUM A-D (loperamide hydrochloride) oral solution: Drug Facts label
org: DailyMed (US National Library of Medicine); labeling supplied by the manufacturer (Kenvue Brands LLC)
licence_note: Manufacturer's FDA-required Drug Facts labeling as posted on DailyMed. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16: do not use if you have bloody or black stool; ask a doctor before use if you have fever or mucus in the stool; children 2-5 years ask a doctor; children under 2 years (up to 33 lbs) do not use; store between 20-25 C (68-77 F).

title: STOP THE BLEED: Frequently Asked Questions and Training pages
org: STOP THE BLEED Program, US Department of Defense (Defense Health Agency)
licence_note: US federal government work. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16: a class runs about one hour (direct pressure, wound packing, tourniquet); if bleeding continues pack the wound; if there is still bleeding apply a tourniquet 2 to 3 inches above the wound and keep tightening until the bleeding stops; warn the person it will hurt; kits contain a tourniquet, packing gauze or hemostatic dressing, a compression bandage, nitrile gloves and a marker; program tourniquets are drawn from the CoTCCC list.

title: Diarrhoeal disease (fact sheet)
licence_note: Copyright WHO. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16: diarrhoeal disease is the third leading cause of death in children under 5 years old; diarrhoea should be treated with oral rehydration solution (ORS), a solution of clean water, sugar and salt; a 10-14 day course of zinc shortens duration; prevention by safe drinking-water, sanitation and hand washing with soap.

title: Hydrocarbon pneumonia
org: MedlinePlus (US National Library of Medicine / NIH)
licence_note: MedlinePlus encyclopedia text licensed from A.D.A.M. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16: drinking or breathing in gasoline, kerosene and other oily hydrocarbons can send some into the lungs (aspiration); symptoms include coughing or grunting respiration, shortness of breath, hydrocarbon smell on the breath, vomiting, blue lips, fever, stupor. It gives no fixed observation period after swallowing.

title: CPR - infant
org: MedlinePlus (US National Library of Medicine / NIH)
licence_note: MedlinePlus encyclopedia text licensed from A.D.A.M.; review date 2/10/2026, citing the 2025 AHA/AAP pediatric BLS guidelines. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16: thumbs side by side with hands encircling the chest just below the nipple line, or the heel of one hand if the chest cannot be compressed far enough; about 1 1/2 inches (4 cm); 100 to 120 a minute; 30:2 one rescuer, 15:2 two rescuers; cover mouth and nose; about 2 minutes of CPR before leaving to call if alone.

title: Non-fatal drowning (first aid)
org: MedlinePlus (US National Library of Medicine / NIH)
licence_note: MedlinePlus encyclopedia text licensed from A.D.A.M.; review date 10/14/2025. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16: if breathing has stopped, begin rescue breathing as soon as you can; once on land give CPR as needed; remove cold wet clothes; the Heimlich maneuver is not part of routine drowning rescue.

title: Part 6: Pediatric Basic Life Support: 2025 American Heart Association and American Academy of Pediatrics Guidelines for CPR and Emergency Cardiovascular Care (Circulation 2025;152(16 suppl 2):S424-S447)
org: American Heart Association and American Academy of Pediatrics
licence_note: Copyright AHA/AAP. Full text refused automated access (403) on 2026-11-16; R15 read the PubMed abstract (PMID 41122891) and the AHA newsroom release: 2-finger infant compressions eliminated, 1-hand or 2 thumb-encircling hands technique recommended (heel of one hand if the chest cannot be encircled); infants with severe choking get repeated cycles of 5 back blows alternating with 5 chest thrusts, no abdominal thrusts; children get 5 back blows alternating with 5 abdominal thrusts.

title: What to Do After a Mild TBI or Concussion
licence_note: US federal government work. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16 (web fetcher; curl refused): resting is good the first few days, when symptoms are more severe; ease back into regular activities; limit screen time and loud music before bed; most people can return to work, school and many other activities within a few days or weeks; talk to a provider if symptoms do not go away or get worse.

title: FRIO Insulin Travel Wallet Instruction Leaflet (English)
org: FRIO (manufacturer of evaporative insulin cooling wallets)
licence_note: Manufacturer's instructions. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16: keeps insulin within 18-26 C (64.4-78.8 F) for 45 hours minimum even at a constant 37.8 C (100 F); re-immerse every 45 hours or sooner if crystals can be felt; soak times by size (Mini 2-3 min to Extra Large 15-19 min), strictly timed because over-soaking renders the wallet unusable until it dries; drain 15-30 minutes and towel dry; not in an airtight or waterproof container; not in a refrigerator or freezer; insulin must be at the maker's recommended temperature before it goes in; drying out takes 2-4 weeks; no washing machine or tumble dryer; with age soak time increases; replace when crystals fail to expand.

title: Maternal mortality (fact sheet)
licence_note: Copyright WHO. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16: the major complications that account for around 75% of maternal deaths are severe bleeding (mostly after childbirth), infections (usually after childbirth), high blood pressure in pregnancy (pre-eclampsia and eclampsia), complications from delivery and unsafe abortion; severe bleeding after birth can kill a healthy woman within hours if she is unattended.

title: Febrile seizures
org: MedlinePlus (US National Library of Medicine / NIH)
licence_note: MedlinePlus encyclopedia text licensed from A.D.A.M.; review date 1/1/2026. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16: most often in otherwise healthy children between 6 months and 5 years; a simple febrile seizure stops by itself within a few seconds to 10 minutes; one lasting longer than 15 minutes, in just one part of the body, or recurring in the same illness is not a normal febrile seizure; turn the child on the side; do not force anything into the mouth; if it lasts several minutes call 911.

title: Croup
org: MedlinePlus (US National Library of Medicine / NIH)
licence_note: MedlinePlus encyclopedia text licensed from A.D.A.M.; review date 1/1/2026. Read by R15 on 2026-11-16: affects children 3 months to 5 years; cool or warm moist air (steamy bathroom or cool night air) may help the child feel better though no studies show it reduces symptoms; call 911 for bluish lips or skin, drooling, trouble swallowing, stridor at rest or getting worse, tugging-in of the muscles between the ribs, or struggling to breathe.
